message.content:
In **Flappy Bird** the scoring system starts counting only when you successfully fly past a pair of pipes.  
So:

| Situation | Score |
|-----------|-------|
| Game just launched – before touching any pipe | **0** |
| You hit the very first obstacle right away | Still **0**, because no pipe has been cleared yet |

Because the counter begins at zero and increases by one per completed set of pipes, *zero* is technically the lowest possible score you can have while playing the game.  

If you’re looking for historical “lowest” records from other players, most public leaderboards simply list the best (highest) scores—there isn’t an official metric for the absolute lowest score beyond the trivial case of failing instantly.
